sanskrit: rocate me vacaḥ kṛtsnaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ rocate yadi yuṣmākaṃ tan mā prabrūta māciram
english: My entire speech pleases the Brāhmaṇas — of this there is no doubt. If it pleases you as well, then tell me so without delay.

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te sarve tathety ūcur narādhipam saṃdideśa tato rājā vyāpārasthān yathākramam
english: Thus addressed, all of them said to the lord of men, "So be it." The king then gave orders to those stationed at their duties, each in proper sequence.

sanskrit: halasya karaṇe cāpi vyādiṣṭāḥ sarvaśilpinaḥ yathoktaṃ ca nṛpaśreṣṭha kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ yathākramam
english: All the craftsmen were also instructed regarding the fashioning of the plough, and, O best of kings, everything was done just as ordered, in proper sequence.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tu śilpinaḥ sarve amātyapravarāś ca ha viduraś ca mahāprājño dhārtarāṣṭre nyavedayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all the craftsmen, together with the foremost ministers, reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, and the greatly wise Vidura announced it.

sanskrit: sajjaṃ kratuvaraṃ rājan kālaprāptaṃ ca bhārata sauvarṇaṃ ca kṛtaṃ divyaṃ lāṅgalaṃ sumahādhanam
english: "O king, O Bharata, the foremost sacrifice is ready; the proper time has come; and the divine golden plough, of immense wealth, has been fashioned."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā nṛpaśreṣṭho dhārtarāṣṭro viśāṃ pate ājñāpayām āsa nṛpaḥ kraturājapravartanam
english: Hearing this, O lord of the people, the best of kings, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, commanded that the king of sacrifices be commenced.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yajñaḥ prabhūtānnaḥ susaṃskṛtaḥ dīkṣitaś cāpi gāndhārir yathāśāstraṃ yathākramam
english: Then the sacrifice commenced — with abundant food, well-performed — and Gāndhārī too was consecrated for initiation according to scripture and in proper order.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭo dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhūd viduraś ca mahāyaśāḥ bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇo gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra was overjoyed, as was the greatly renowned Vidura, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, and the illustrious Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: nimantraṇārthaṃ dūtāṃś ca preṣayām āsa śīghragān pārthivānāṃ ca rājendra brāhmaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca te prayātā yathoddiṣṭaṃ dūtās tvaritavāhanāḥ
english: He also dispatched swift messengers to invite kings and Brāhmaṇas alike, O king of kings; those envoys with swift mounts departed to their assigned destinations.

sanskrit: tatra kaṃ cit prayātaṃ tu dūtaṃ duḥśāsano 'bravīt gaccha dvaitavanaṃ śīghraṃ pāṇḍavān pāpapūruṣān nimantraya yathānyāyaṃ viprāṃs tasmin mahāvane
english: Then Duḥśāsana addressed one of the departing envoys: "Go quickly to the Dvaita forest; invite the sinful Pāṇḍavas in the proper manner, as well as the Brāhmaṇas in that great forest."

sanskrit: sa gatvā pāṇḍavāvāsam uvācābhipraṇamya tān duryodhano mahārāja yajate nṛpasattamaḥ
english: That messenger went to the dwelling of the Pāṇḍavas, bowed to them, and said, "O great king, Duryodhana, the best of kings, is performing a sacrifice."

sanskrit: svavīryārjitam arthaugham avāpya kurunandanaḥ tatra gacchanti rājāno brāhmaṇāś ca tatas tataḥ
english: "Having acquired great wealth by his own valour, the joy of the Kurus is holding it; kings and Brāhmaṇas are coming from all directions to attend."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu preṣito rājan kauraveṇa mahātmanā āmantrayati vo rājā dhārtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ mano 'bhilaṣitaṃ rājñas taṃ kratuṃ draṣṭum arhatha
english: "I have been sent, O king, by the great-souled Kaurava; the king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, invites you — you should come to witness that sacrifice which is the king's heart's desire."

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā tac chrutvā dūtabhāṣitam abravīn nṛpaśārdūlo diṣṭyā rājā suyodhanaḥ yajate kratumukhyena pūrveṣāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ
english: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira, tiger among kings, having heard what the envoy said, replied: "By good fortune king Suyodhana performs the foremost of sacrifices, he who enhances the glory of his ancestors."

sanskrit: vayam apy upayāsyāmo na tv idānīṃ kathaṃ cana samayaḥ paripālyo no yāvad varṣaṃ trayodaśam
english: "We too shall come, but not now, under any circumstances — our pledge must be kept until thirteen years have passed."

sanskrit: śrutvaitad dharmarājasya bhīmo vacanam abravīt tadā tu nṛpatir gantā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having heard this, Bhīma then spoke these words: "Indeed, king Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira will go —

sanskrit: astraśastrapradīpte 'gnau yadā taṃ pātayiṣyati varṣāt trayodaśād ūrdhvaṃ raṇasatre narādhipaḥ
english: — when that lord of men, in the fire blazing with weapons and missiles, will cast him into it at a war-sacrifice after thirteen years have elapsed.

sanskrit: yadā krodhahavir moktā dhārtarāṣṭreṣu pāṇḍavaḥ āgantāras tadā smeti vācyas te sa suyodhanaḥ
english: When the Pāṇḍava releases the oblation of his wrath upon the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — then you should tell that Suyodhana: 'They will come.'"

sanskrit: śeṣās tu pāṇḍavā rājan naivocuḥ kiṃ cid apriyam dūtaś cāpi yathāvṛttaṃ dhārtarāṣṭre nyavedayat
english: The remaining Pāṇḍavas, O king, spoke nothing disagreeable. And the envoy reported the whole matter as it had transpired to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: athājagmur naraśreṣṭhā nānājanapadeśvarāḥ brāhmaṇāś ca mahābhāgā dhārtarāṣṭrapuraṃ prati
english: Then came the best of men, lords of various kingdoms, and greatly blessed Brāhmaṇas, all heading toward the city of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: te tv arcitā yathāśāstraṃ yathāvarṇaṃ yathākramam mudā paramayā yuktāḥ prītyā cāpi nareśvara
english: They were honored according to scripture, according to their station, and in proper order, with the greatest joy and affection, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro 'pi rājendra saṃvṛtaḥ sarvakauravaiḥ harṣeṇa mahatā yukto viduraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra too, O king of kings, surrounded by all the Kauravas, filled with great delight, spoke to Vidura:

sanskrit: yathā sukhī janaḥ sarvaḥ kṣattaḥ syād annasaṃyutaḥ tuṣyec ca yajñasadane tathā kṣipraṃ vidhīyatām
english: "See to it at once, O Kṣattā, that all the people be happy and well-provided with food, and that they be satisfied in the hall of sacrifice."

sanskrit: viduras tv evam ājñaptaḥ sarvavarṇān ariṃdama yathāpramāṇato vidvān pūjayām āsa dharmavit
english: Thus commanded, Vidura, O crusher of foes, the wise knower of dharma, honored all the social orders in due measure.

sanskrit: bhakṣyabhojyānnapānena mālyaiś cāpi sugandhibhiḥ vāsobhir vividhaiś caiva yojayām āsa hṛṣṭavat
english: He supplied them with things to eat and drink, food and beverages, with fragrant garlands, and with garments of many kinds — all with a joyful heart.

sanskrit: kṛtvā hy avabhṛthaṃ vīro yathāśāstraṃ yathākramam sāntvayitvā ca rājendro dattvā ca vividhaṃ vasu visarjayām āsa nṛpān brāhmaṇāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: After the hero duly performed the concluding ablution according to scripture and in proper order, the king of kings, having consoled them and given them various riches, dismissed the kings and Brāhmaṇas in their thousands.

sanskrit: visarjayitvā sa nṛpān bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ viveśa hāstinapuraṃ sahitaḥ karṇasaubalaiḥ
english: Having dismissed the kings, he entered Hāstinapura surrounded by his brothers, together with Karṇa and the son of Subala.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca praviśantaṃ mahārāja sūtās tuṣṭuvur acyutam janāś cāpi maheṣvāsaṃ tuṣṭuvū rājasattamam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As he entered, O great king, bards praised the unshakeable one; the people too praised that great archer, the best of kings.

sanskrit: lājaiś candanacūrṇaiś cāpy avakīrya janās tadā ūcur diṣṭyā nṛpāvighnāt samāpto 'yaṃ kratus tava
english: Strewing parched rice and sandalwood powder upon him, the people then said: "By good fortune this sacrifice of yours has been completed without obstacle, O king."

sanskrit: apare tv abruvaṃs tatra vātikās taṃ mahīpatim yudhiṣṭhirasya yajñena na samo hy eṣa tu kratuḥ naiva tasya krator eṣa kalām arhati ṣoḍaśīm
english: But others among the gossipers there spoke to that lord of the earth: "This sacrifice is not equal to Yudhiṣṭhira's sacrifice — it does not merit even a sixteenth part of that one."

sanskrit: evaṃ tatrābruvan ke cid vātikās taṃ nareśvaram suhṛdas tv abruvaṃs tatra ati sarvān ayaṃ kratuḥ
english: Thus did some gossips speak there to that lord of men; but his friends said there: "This sacrifice surpasses all."

sanskrit: yayātir nahuṣaś cāpi māndhātā bharatas tathā kratum enaṃ samāhṛtya pūtāḥ sarve divaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Yayāti, Nahuṣa, Māndhātā, and Bharata — all were purified by performing this sacrifice and went to heaven."

sanskrit: etā vācaḥ śubhāḥ śṛṇvan suhṛdāṃ bharatarṣabha praviveśa puraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ svaveśma ca narādhipaḥ
english: Hearing these auspicious words of his friends, O bull of the Bharatas, the lord of men entered the city joyfully and then his own palace.

sanskrit: abhivādya tataḥ pādau mātāpitror viśāṃ pate bhīṣmadroṇakṛpāṇāṃ ca vidurasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: Then, O lord of the people, he bowed at the feet of his mother and father, and also of Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the wise Vidura.

sanskrit: abhivāditaḥ kanīyobhir bhrātṛbhir bhrātṛvatsalaḥ niṣasādāsane mukhye bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Greeted by his younger brothers, that affectionate elder brother took his seat on the foremost throne, surrounded by his brothers.

sanskrit: tam utthāya mahārāja sūtaputro 'bravīd vacaḥ diṣṭyā te bharataśreṣṭha samāpto 'yaṃ mahākratuḥ
english: Rising before him, O great king, the son of the charioteer spoke these words: "By good fortune, O best of the Bharatas, this great sacrifice of yours has been completed."

sanskrit: hateṣu yudhi pārtheṣu rājasūye tathā tvayā āhṛte 'haṃ naraśreṣṭha tvāṃ sabhājayitā punaḥ
english: "When the sons of Pṛthā have been slain in battle, and the Rājasūya has been performed by you, I shall honour you again, O best of men."

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahārājo dhārtarāṣṭro mahāyaśāḥ satyam etat tvayā vīra pāṇḍaveṣu durātmasu
english: The greatly renowned great king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, said to him: "What you say is true, O hero, regarding those wicked-souled Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: nihateṣu naraśreṣṭha prāpte cāpi mahākratau rājasūye punar vīra tvaṃ māṃ saṃvardhayiṣyasi
english: "When they have been slain, O best of men, and when the great Rājasūya sacrifice has been obtained, you will exalt me again, O hero."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahāprājñaḥ karṇam āśliṣya bhārata rājasūyaṃ kratuśreṣṭhaṃ cintayām āsa kauravaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the greatly wise Kaurava embraced Karṇa, O Bharata, and began to contemplate the Rājasūya, the best of sacrifices.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt suhṛdaś cāpi pārśvasthān nṛpasattamaḥ kadā tu taṃ kratuvaraṃ rājasūyaṃ mahādhanam nihatya pāṇḍavān sarvān āhariṣyāmi kauravāḥ
english: He also spoke to his friends standing nearby, that best of kings: "When shall I, O Kauravas, slay all the Pāṇḍavas and perform that foremost sacrifice, the great Rājasūya, of immense wealth?"

sanskrit: tam abravīt tadā karṇaḥ śṛṇu me rājakuñjara pādau na dhāvaye tāvad yāvan na nihato 'rjunaḥ
english: Then Karṇa said to him: "Hear me, O elephant among kings — I shall not wash my feet until Arjuna has been slain."

sanskrit: athotkruṣṭaṃ maheṣvāsair dhārtarāṣṭrair mahārathaiḥ pratijñāte phalgunasya vadhe karṇena saṃyuge vijitāṃś cāpy amanyanta pāṇḍavān dhṛtarāṣṭrajāḥ
english: Then there arose shouts of acclaim from the great bowmen, the great chariot-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons; when Karṇa had pledged the slaying of Phalguna in battle, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra considered the Pāṇḍavas already vanquished.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi rājendra visṛjya narapuṃgavān praviveśa gṛhaṃ śrīmān yathā caitrarathaṃ prabhuḥ te 'pi sarve maheṣvāsā jagmur veśmāni bhārata
english: Duryodhana too, O king of kings, dismissing those bull-like men, the glorious lord entered his home like the lord entering the Chaitraratha forest. And all those great bowmen also went to their dwellings, O Bharata.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca maheṣvāsā dūtavākyapracoditāḥ cintayantas tam evārthaṃ nālabhanta sukhaṃ kva cit
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, those great bowmen, stirred up by the envoy's words, thinking on that very matter, found no peace anywhere.

sanskrit: bhūyaś ca cārai rājendra pravṛttir upapāditā pratijñā sūtaputrasya vijayasya vadhaṃ prati
english: And again through spies, O king of kings, news was brought of the pledge of the charioteer's son regarding the slaying of Vijaya.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā dharmasutaḥ samudvigno narādhipa abhedyakavacaṃ matvā karṇam adbhutavikramam anusmaraṃś ca saṃkleśān na śāntim upayāti saḥ
english: Hearing this, the son of Dharma was deeply agitated, O lord of men; considering Karṇa with his impenetrable armour to be of wondrous valour, and remembering his own sufferings, he found no peace.

sanskrit: tasya cintāparītasya buddhir jajñe mahātmanaḥ bahuvyālamṛgākīrṇaṃ tyaktuṃ dvaitavanaṃ vanam
english: In his mind oppressed by anxiety, the thought arose in that great soul to leave the Dvaita forest, teeming with many snakes and wild beasts.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭro 'pi nṛpatiḥ praśaśāsa vasuṃdharām bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito vīrair bhīṣmadroṇakṛpais tathā
english: The king, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, for his part, ruled the earth together with his heroic brothers and with Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Kṛpa.

sanskrit: saṃgamya sūtaputreṇa karṇenāhavaśobhinā duryodhanaḥ priye nityaṃ vartamāno mahīpatiḥ pūjayām āsa viprendrān kratubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: Meeting with the son of the charioteer, Karṇa, who was resplendent in battle, Duryodhana the lord of the earth, ever abiding in what was dear to him, honoured the foremost Brāhmaṇas with sacrifices bearing lavish sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ ca priyaṃ rājan sa cakāra paraṃtapaḥ niścitya manasā vīro dattabhuktaphalaṃ dhanam
english: He also did what was pleasing to his brothers, O king, that scourge of enemies; the hero, having resolved in his mind, distributed wealth the fruit of which was giving and enjoyment.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca duryodhanaṃ mocayitvā pāṇḍuputrā mahābalāḥ kim akārṣur vane tasmiṃs tan mamākhyātum arhasi
english: Janamejaya said: After freeing Duryodhana, what did the mighty sons of Pāṇḍu do in that forest? Please tell me this.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śayānaṃ kaunteyaṃ rātrau dvaitavane mṛgāḥ svapnānte darśayām āsur bāṣpakaṇṭhā yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then at night in the Dvaita forest, the deer appeared to the sleeping son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, at the end of a dream, their voices choked with tears.

sanskrit: tān abravīt sa rājendro vepamānān kṛtāñjalīn brūta yad vaktukāmāḥ stha ke bhavantaḥ kim iṣyate
english: That king of kings said to them, trembling with hands joined in supplication: "Speak what you wish to say. Who are you? What is desired?"

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ pāṇḍavena kaunteyena yaśasvinā pratyabruvan mṛgās tatra hataśeṣā yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Thus addressed by the glorious Pāṇḍava, the son of Kuntī, the deer — the survivors of the slaughter — spoke there to Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: vayaṃ mṛgā dvaitavane hataśiṣṭāḥ sma bhārata notsīdema mahārāja kriyatāṃ vāsaparyayaḥ
english: "We are the deer of the Dvaita forest, O Bharata, the survivors of the killing. Let us not perish utterly, O great king — let there be a change of dwelling."

sanskrit: bhavanto bhrātaraḥ śūrāḥ sarva evāstrakovidāḥ kulāny alpāvaśiṣṭāni kṛtavanto vanaukasām
english: "You brothers are heroes, all of you skilled in weapons, and you have reduced the families of forest dwellers to only a few survivors."

sanskrit: bījabhūtā vayaṃ ke cid avaśiṣṭā mahāmate vivardhemahi rājendra prasādāt te yudhiṣṭhira
english: "We who remain are but seed-animals, O great-minded one; through your grace, O king of kings, O Yudhiṣṭhira, may we multiply again."

sanskrit: tān vepamānān vitrastān bījamātrāvaśeṣitān mṛgān dṛṣṭvā suduḥkhārto dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Seeing those deer trembling, terrified, only seed-animals left in number, king Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira was deeply pained.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathety abravīd rājā sarvabhūtahite rataḥ tathyaṃ bhavanto bruvate kariṣyāmi ca tat tathā
english: The king who was devoted to the welfare of all beings said to them: "So be it. What you say is true, and I shall do exactly that."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ pratibuddhaḥ sa rātryante rājasattamaḥ abravīt sahitān bhrātṝn dayāpanno mṛgān prati
english: Thus having awakened at the end of the night, that best of kings, filled with compassion for the deer, spoke to his brothers assembled together:

sanskrit: ukto rātrau mṛgair asmi svapnānte hataśeṣitaiḥ tanubhūtāḥ sma bhadraṃ te dayā naḥ kriyatām iti
english: "I have been spoken to at night by the deer, those who remain after the killing, at the end of a dream: 'We have become few; blessings on you — show compassion to us.'"

sanskrit: te satyam āhuḥ kartavyā dayāsmābhir vanaukasām sāṣṭamāsaṃ hi no varṣaṃ yad enān upayuñjmahe
english: "They speak the truth; we must show compassion to the forest creatures — for we have been consuming them for nearly eight months now throughout the year."

sanskrit: punar bahumṛgaṃ ramyaṃ kāmyakaṃ kānanottamam marubhūmeḥ śiraḥ khyātaṃ tṛṇabindusaraḥ prati tatremā vasatīḥ śiṣṭā viharanto ramemahi
english: "Let us go again to Kāmyaka, that delightful forest with many deer, the best of forests, famed as the head of the desert land, toward the lake of Tṛṇabindu — let us dwell in those abodes that remain and take pleasure roaming there."

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavāḥ śīghraṃ prayayur dharmakovidāḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ sahitā rājan ye ca tatra sahoṣitāḥ indrasenādibhiś caiva preṣyair anugatās tadā
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, versed in dharma, quickly departed together with the Brāhmaṇas, O king, and those who had dwelt there with them, and followed by servants headed by Indrasena.

sanskrit: te yātvānusṛtair mārgaiḥ svannaiḥ śucijalānvitaiḥ dadṛśuḥ kāmyakaṃ puṇyam āśramaṃ tāpasāyutam
english: Traveling along well-trodden paths with good food and pure water, they beheld the holy Kāmyaka hermitage filled with ascetics.

sanskrit: viviśus te sma kauravyā vṛtā viprarṣabhais tadā tad vanaṃ bharataśreṣṭhāḥ svargaṃ sukṛtino yathā
english: Those descendants of Kuru, O best of the Bharatas, surrounded by foremost Brāhmaṇas, entered that forest like the virtuous entering heaven.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vane nivasatāṃ teṣāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām varṣāṇy ekādaśātīyuḥ kṛcchreṇa bharatarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: For those great-souled Pāṇḍavas dwelling in the forest, eleven years passed in hardship, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanās te hi sukhārhā duḥkham uttamam prāptakālam anudhyāntaḥ sehur uttamapūruṣāḥ
english: Subsisting on fruits and roots, those best of men, though worthy of happiness, endured the greatest suffering, meditating on the time that had yet to come.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu rājarṣir ātmakarmāparādhajam cintayan sa mahābāhur bhrātṝṇāṃ duḥkham uttamam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, the royal sage, long-armed, reflected on the supreme suffering of his brothers, born of his own actions and transgressions.

sanskrit: na suṣvāpa sukhaṃ rājā hṛdi śalyair ivārpitaiḥ daurātmyam anupaśyaṃs tat kāle dyūtodbhavasya hi
english: The king slept not happily, his heart as if pierced by arrows, beholding that wickedness which had arisen from the dice-game at that fateful time.

sanskrit: saṃsmaran paruṣā vācaḥ sūtaputrasya pāṇḍavaḥ niḥśvāsaparamo dīno bibhrat kopaviṣaṃ mahat
english: Recalling the harsh words of the charioteer's son, the Pāṇḍava, wretched, breathing heavy sighs, bore within him a great poison of wrath.

sanskrit: arjuno yamajau cobhau draupadī ca yaśasvinī sa ca bhīmo mahātejāḥ sarveṣām uttamo balī yudhiṣṭhiram udīkṣantaḥ sehur duḥkham anuttamam
english: Arjuna, the twin brothers, the illustrious Draupadī, and Bhīma of great energy, the mightiest of all — looking to Yudhiṣṭhira, they endured unparalleled suffering.

sanskrit: avaśiṣṭam alpakālaṃ manvānāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ vapur anyad ivākārṣur utsāhāmarṣaceṣṭitaiḥ
english: Those bulls among men, considering that only a little time remained, bore themselves as if in a different body through the exertions of zeal and indignation.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ ājagāma mahāyogī pāṇḍavān avalokakaḥ
english: Then after some time, Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, the great yogin, came to visit the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pratyudgamya mahātmānaṃ pratyagṛhṇād yathāvidhi
english: Seeing him arrive, Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira went forth to meet that great soul and received him with due ceremony.

sanskrit: tam āsīnam upāsīnaḥ śuśrūṣur niyatendriyaḥ toṣayan praṇipātena vyāsaṃ pāṇḍavanandanaḥ
english: Sitting near him once he was seated, the son who was the joy of the Pāṇḍavas attended on Vyāsa with disciplined senses, pleasing him with obeisance.

sanskrit: tān avekṣya kṛśān pautrān vane vanyena jīvataḥ maharṣir anukampārtham abravīd bāṣpagadgadam
english: Seeing those emaciated grandsons living in the forest on forest fare, the great seer, out of compassion, spoke with a voice choked by tears:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho śṛṇu dharmabhṛtāṃ vara nātaptatapasaḥ putra prāpnuvanti mahat sukham
english: "O Yudhiṣṭhira, long-armed, O best of those who uphold dharma, hear me — those who have not undergone austerity, my son, do not attain great happiness."

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe hi puruṣaḥ paryāyeṇopasevate nātyantam asukhaṃ kaś cit prāpnoti puruṣarṣabha
english: "For a man experiences happiness and suffering in alternation; no one endures absolute unhappiness forever, O bull among men."
